newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks rise on Greenspan testimony, curbs set.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks rise on Greenspan testimony, curbs set.

text.p: Wall Street shares rose to just below session highs on Tuesday, while Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan began delivering his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on the economy to Congress.

The Dow Jones Industrial average was up around 105 points at 8011. It extended gains minutes before the prepared text of Greenspan's speech were released, prompting the New York Stock Exchange to set curbs on index-arbitrage trading.
The Fed chief said in a prepared text that the Federal Reserve must be ready to act if necessary to head off inflation but for now, economic growth seemed to be slowing.
The long bond, which also started to gain before the text was released, rose 25/32 to yield 6.48 percent.
The Nasdaq composite, which had suffered profit-taking recently, added around 15 points to 1551.

In his semi-annual, mandatory testimony to Congress, Greenspan said: "I have no doubt that the current stance of policy...will need to be changed at some point....For the present, demand growth does appear to have moderated."
He said in his prepared text that stock market gains could fuel demand in the future.
